rationale: Pathfinder is a compute-bound A*-style graph search proxy app (searchAlgorithms.c, vectorUtils.c, node.c dominate; ~19.5 KB text, 97 functions), with timing instrumentation (gettime.c), so heavy control-flow passes must be gated by strong runtime-cost weights: BCF and FLA get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain (they most disrupt static recovery of the recursive search and parsing dispatch logic) but the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so they are steered away from hot inner loops and toward cold, large functions like parseFile/parseConfigFile/main where their footprint is affordable; FLA carries the highest CorrectnessRisk since flattening recursive-search and vector-math control flow is where semantic breakage is most likely in this codebase. SUB and SPLIT are nearly free (low cost weights, low risk) and are left broadly applicable to build baseline structural noise across all 97 functions cheaply. IBR and ICALL are kept at moderate cost weights with elevated CorrectnessRisk because Pathfinder's performance-critical call sites (node/graph updates inside the search loop) are sensitive to indirect-call and branch overhead and to any mis-binding of indirect targets; IGV is enabled moderately to obscure the configuration/system-call-map lookup tables, which are data-oriented reverse-engineering anchors, at low risk. Net effect: cheap passes everywhere, expensive passes concentrated on cold, large, parsing/statistics code, preserving search-loop throughput and correctness.
